349272.title: Odd-power symmetric sum conjecture
349272.statement:
Let $m\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $x$ be a positive integer. The coefficients ${\mathbf{A}}_{m,0}, {\mathbf{A}}_{m,1},\ldots,{\mathbf{A}}_{m,m}$ are constants independent of $x$ and $k$. **Odd-power symmetric sum conjecture.** For every $m\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist coefficients ${\mathbf{A}}_{m,0}, {\mathbf{A}}_{m,1},\ldots,{\mathbf{A}}_{m,m}$ such that

$$
x^{2m+1}=\sum_{k=1}^{x}\left({\mathbf{A}}_{m,0}k^0(x-k)^0+{\mathbf{A}}_{m,1}(x-k)^1+{\mathbf{A}}_{m,2}k^2(x-k)^2+\cdots+{\mathbf{A}}_{m,m}k^m(x-k)^m\right).
$$

The claim proposes a generalization of the displayed decomposition of $x^3$ as a sum of symmetric terms involving $k$ and $x-k$. The source does not provide a resolution or further conditions on the coefficients, so its status remains open.
349272.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1909.07269](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.07269), [arXiv:1712.08666](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.08666), [arXiv:1504.05482](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.05482).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.00227

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).
349272.source_name: Petro Kolosov, “An unusual identity for odd-powers”, arXiv:2101.00227 (2021).

375268.title: Odd-index period formula conjecture for the family $1(01)^k$
375268.statement:
Consider the family of finite configurations whose current binary word is $1(01)^k$, with period function $P(k)$ assigning to the configuration indexed by $k$ its period. 

**Odd-index period formula conjecture.** The period function satisfies

$$
P(2i+1)=4^{2i+3}-1
$$

for $i\in\mathbb{N}$.
The formula is suggested by computational experiments, and the source explicitly says that it is suspected to hold for every $i\in\mathbb{N}$; no proof or resolution is given.
375268.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2606.02792](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.02792), [arXiv:2101.09027](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.09027), [arXiv:0910.1258](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1258).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13159

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).
375268.source_name: Enrico Formenti and Supreeti Kamylia, “The Curious Case of Reversible Elementary Second Order Cellular Automaton 115”, arXiv:2606.13159 (2026).

375269.title: Even-index period formula conjecture for the family $1(01)^k$
375269.statement:
Consider the family of finite configurations whose current binary word is $1(01)^k$, with period function $P(k)$ assigning to the configuration indexed by $k$ its period. 

**Even-index period formula conjecture.** The period function satisfies

$$
P(2i)=\frac{2\cdot4^{2i+2}-7\cdot4^{i+1}+5}{3}
$$

for $i\in\mathbb{N}$.
This formula is inferred from experimentally observed base-$4$ patterns for the periods at even indices; the source presents it as a conjectural formula and gives no proof or resolution.
375269.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2102.06956](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.06956), [arXiv:2008.01480](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.01480), [arXiv:0910.1258](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1258).

365404.title: Monotonicity conjecture for hook counts in t-regular partitions
365404.statement:
For integers $t\geq2$ and $k\geq1$, let $b_{t,k}(n)$ denote the number of hooks of length $k$ in all $t$-regular partitions of $n$. A $t$-regular partition is a partition with no part divisible by $t$.

**Monotonicity conjecture.** Let $t\geq3$ be an integer. Then

$$
b_{t+1,2}(n)\geq b_{t,2}(n),
$$

for all $n\geq0$.

The conjecture formalizes numerical evidence that the number of hooks of length $2$ in $t$-regular partitions increases with $t$. The source gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
365404.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2006.07704](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.07704), [arXiv:1808.01416](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.01416).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.15088

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).
365404.source_name: Gurinder Singh and Rupam Barman, “Hook length inequalities for t-regular partitions in the t-aspect”, arXiv:2410.15088 (2025).

358587.title: Bašić et al.'s existence conjecture for circulant nut graphs of degree divisible by four
358587.statement: A **circulant nut graph** is a circulant graph whose adjacency matrix has a one-dimensional null space spanned by a full vector. Let $d$ be a degree satisfying $d \equiv_4 0$, and let $n$ be even with $n \ge d+4$. **Bašić et al.'s conjecture.** For every such $d$ and $n$, there exists a circulant nut graph of order $n$ and degree $d$. The conjecture gives a sufficient existence condition matching the necessary condition for vertex-transitive nut graphs in the case that the degree is divisible by four; its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.
358587.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2212.03026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.03026), [arXiv:2210.08334](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.08334), [arXiv:2102.04418](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.04418).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18658

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2023).
358587.source_name: Ivan Damnjanović, “A note on Cayley nut graphs whose degree is divisible by four”, arXiv:2305.18658 (2023).
